steps.referenceSource: INDEPENDENT ORACLE, NOT AN AURORA-TO-AURORA BASELINE: this frame is rendered by Microsoft Edge, captured on 2026-10-17 with `"C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\Edge\Application\msedge.exe" --headless=new --force-device-scale-factor=1 --window-size=1280,638 --hide-scrollbars --no-first-run --no-default-browser-check --screenshot=aurora-browser/tests/reference/flow-sizing.edge.png file:///<repo>/aurora-browser/tests/reference/flow-sizing.html`. The fixture holds six real-flow sizing cases in six absolutely positioned cells, each a solid rectangle so that no glyph can decide a pixel, at the engine's own 1280x638 page viewport and 1x device scale: (1) two adjacent block siblings whose 20px bottom and 30px top margins must collapse to 30px, with the first child's 10px top margin staying inside its formatting-context cell; (2) a 50% width resolving against the padded containing block's CONTENT box, 130px and not 150px; (3) min-width clamping a 100px used width up to 160px and max-width clamping 300px down to 120px; (4) a shrink-to-fit inline-block taking its widest content (80px) with the next one (60px) beside it on the same line; (5) two left floats sharing one line, with a clear:left block starting below the taller 60px float; (6) a fixed table layout giving 25% and 75% of a 300px table to one column each. The engine renders the same fixture through aurora-browser/tests/pageshot-probe.d --fixture at the same 1280x638 viewport (no app chrome, no scaling), and the two frames are compared pixel-for-pixel with channelTolerance 0.
